cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's Audit Machine test the year-end cash of HANGS Construction Services.
It recomputes cash from every line of the ledger and the bank reconciliations.
Materiality, the size of error that matters, is $340,000.
The bank reports about $188,000 more than the books.
Now it matches every June payment to the bank statement and redoes the reconciliations.
One old check was never cashed, and $4,065 of bank charges were never recorded.
Cut-off: is each receipt and payment in the right year? Yes, and no cash is held back.
Now it adds up what it found and sets it against materiality.
Then it writes the workpapers and a draft findings memo for the CPA.

All done. The gap with the bank is fully explained. The one error in income is $4,065 of bank charges, well under materiality. Eight items stay open, including two reconciliations no one has reviewed. The CPA, a person, concludes and signs. The machine gives no opinion.
